median.rtt_why: 12 Mbit/s is the only value in the sweep cited AS a median that is not the best-carrier figure, so it is the median cell's uplink; 13.6 is NOT used here because the ruling's own correction says it is the optimistic end. RTT 44 ms is the sweep's middle value and keeps continuity with the main operating point. THE ALTERNATIVE IS OPEN: the sweep's cited median RTT is 22 ms, which is 3.6x below this study's OBSERVED PINGAVG p50 of 80 ms, so a 'median' RTT could defensibly be 22 (cited), 44 (continuity) or 80 (observed). 44 is the default here and the choice is flagged, not hidden.

mixed_fleet.rtt_why: each class takes the sweep RTT that goes with its end of the range. PAIRING A RATE WITH AN RTT IS CONSTRUCTED: the sweep is a full 5x3 grid and records no joint distribution, and the Irish dataset gives no measured bandwidth-RTT pairing for an uplink either.

sweep_values_not_used.why: 13.6 is the main operating point itself, so using it as a class would make a third of the mixed fleet identical to the uniform condition; 25 Mbit/s carries no source in the sweep's citation block and the fast class already has the cited 88 Mbit/s

poor.definition: every device at the sweep's slowest uplink with its tail RTT
poor.expected_scale: at 5 Mbit/s one 63,898 B dashcam JPEG serialises in 0.1022 s and arrives 0.1733 s after capture on an idle uplink (RTT 142 ms); the N1 probe measured the arithmetic at 0.9 Mbit/s, where the same frame takes 0.568 s and 16 devices SATURATE the uplink to a 6.34 s median, so saturation at 5 Mbit/s must be measured, not assumed

poor.rtt_why: 142 ms is the sweep's tail RTT and the poor cell is the tail condition. D215 asks for p99 beside it: this study's OBSERVED PINGAVG p90 is 120 ms and p99 is 351 ms, so the sweep's 142 ms sits between the observed p90 and p99 and is the conservative-but-not-extreme choice.
